newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Volvo strike in Brazil enters 3rd day.
newsitem.headline: Volvo strike in Brazil enters 3rd day.

text.p: A strike by hundreds of workers at Swedish automaker Volvo AB's Brazil unit entered its third day Thursday with a judge poised to rule on the legality of the stoppage, a company spokesman said.
"Production is still paralyzed," said Walter Viapiana, chief spokesman for Volvo in Brazil.
Viapiana also said a labor court judge was slated to rule at 1400 local/1600 GMT today on the legality of the strike by 300 to 700 production-line workers.
Volvo workers had been scheduled to return to work last Tuesday after a 24-day year-end break but decided to strike instead over wages.

The company had asked the Regional Labor Tribunal to rule the strike illegal on the grounds that workers did not notify the company 48 hours in advance and did not follow strike rules laid in Brazilian law.
If the judge finds the strike illegal, workers will have to return to their jobs Friday, Viapiana said.
The company employs 1,400 workers at its plant in Parana state. Brazil is Volvo's second- and fourth-largest market for buses and trucks respectively.
